faq_plan.q: What is a chemical peel consent form?
How do I create a chemical peel consent form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is downloadable chemical peel consent PDFs (ASCP's member sample, day spa and esthetician practice forms) plus one form-builder template: a sheet signed once and filed. This page shows what the clinic runs around the signature once the form is an app: a short re-confirmation on each visit of a peel series, one form shared by three locations with each location's own list, a day-3 check-in that lands on the consent record, and a lobby tablet that clears after every client. The consent wording stays with the clinic's provider or lawyer; the page makes no claim about peel risks, skin reactions, who may perform peels or whether a signature makes consent valid, and quotes MedlinePlus only for what written informed consent is.
tab_stories: At Briarcliff Skin Studio, Lenora Henrikson bought a series of 6 peels and signed the full consent at visit 1; before visit 3 she answers 2 confirmation questions instead of the whole form, and her record shows visit 3 of 6 confirmed.

Fernwell Med Spa runs one consent form at 3 locations: the client picks Riverside, Northgate or Elm Street, and Northgate manager Gisela Brookhart's screen lists the 14 forms signed at Northgate this week out of 41 across all 3.

At Halcyon Aesthetics, Nadira Sefton gets a 3-question check-in email 3 days after her peel, answers yes to a call from her provider, and esthetician Faustine Delacey gets an email card saying Nadira asked for a call.

At Celandine Skin Bar, a client who arrives without a signed form signs on the lobby tablet; Zelda Corrigan at the front desk sees 8 of 9 Saturday clients signed, and the tablet clears the form for the next client after each signature.
